fields.reasoning: The question says the transcript persists on disk, and the Claude adapter already starts each session with a stored --session-id (claudecode.go:57). Resuming that session keeps the agent's context and the work it already committed, so the run does not redo finished steps. A fresh session would lose that context and need a re-briefing. The fresh-session fallback covers the case where the transcript is gone. Nothing in the adapter needs a new ID scheme for this. It departs from engine-orchestrates (agent steps are short, fresh sessions) only for a session that hit the usage limit, so the rule stays for every other step.
fields.statement: Resume a usage-limited run by continuing the same agent session with the Claude CLI's resume flag, keyed on the session ID the run already stores; start a fresh session only when the transcript is missing. This is the one exception to engine-orchestrates: a step's agent session stays open across a usage-limit pause

ops.note: Exception to engine-orchestrates: a usage-limited step resumes its agent session after the pause instead of starting a fresh one
